pr_title: Process incoming frames before sending frames for Http2Connection.
pr_body:
Moves the ProcessIncomingFramesAsync method before sending the preface.
This fixes a deadlock when using a NamedPipe as a transport where
incoming frames need to be read before being able to write.
Also rename _expectingSettingsAck to _receivedSettingsAck to clearly
specify that the settings frame has being received.

Fix #73097

issue_context.title: Http2Connection over async NamedPipe transport hangs when writing preface when Server is waiting for the client to Synchronize.
comments: @dotnet/area-system-io is it expected that the first `WriteAsync` on a `NamedPipeClientStream` would block until a concurrent read is also issued?
That may depend on size of the write and size of socket buffer IMHO. If amount of data exceed the socket buffer there is not good way how to complete the write IMHO.
Right, I'm just surprised in this case since we're talking about only ~60 bytes of data (plus TLS overhead).

> is it expected that the first WriteAsync on a NamedPipeClientStream would block until a concurrent read is also issued?

The synchronous call to WriteAsync blocks, or the WriteAsync synchronous call returns immediately but the returned task doesn't complete until the data is read?  The former is not expected.  The latter is likely.

Because it's not apparent what is going on (the error message says the HTTP/2 connection handshake timed out without any indication why), and the workaround is quite involved, it's unlikely that someone will come up with this solution without spending a lot of time on it.

There is value in .NET+HTTP/2+named pipes just working. And it brings .NET into parity with golang.

It would be great if some changes could be made to HttpClient's Http2Connection to support it.

> This would be the proposed change that I could send a PR for. Move ProcessIncomingFramesAsync from line 244 to line 224
> 
> ```cs
> _ = ProcessIncomingFramesAsync();
> await _stream.WriteAsync(_outgoingBuffer.ActiveMemory, cancellationToken).ConfigureAwait(false);
> ```

I think the line setting `_expectingSettingsAck` to true would need to move before the call to `ProcessIncomingFramesAsync` to avoid a race:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/1dc6524d3d4dc9ba2b661ffd9689dcca6bcebf55/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/SocketsHttpHandler/Http2Connection.cs#L229

IMO easier to invert the name, _expectingSettingsAck renamed to _receivedSettingsAck, leave it as false and set to true when the settings frame is received. Its purpose is checking for multiple SETTINGS frames.

> The synchronous call to WriteAsync blocks, or the WriteAsync synchronous call returns immediately but the returned task doesn't complete until the data is read?

I haven't tried the repro to see which, but the observable behavior would be pretty much the same in this case.

What I am confused by here is that we are talking about requiring reads in order for writes to complete **on the same side of the pipe**. If this is the case, wouldn't all other protocols (e.g. HTTP/1.1) be broken in the same fashion?

> If this is the case, wouldn't all other protocols (e.g. HTTP/1.1) be broken in the same fashion?

Presumably the common case for HTTP/1.1 is for the server to always read before writing and the client to always write before reading.  If the server were to ignore the request and simply write out a response, you'd likely hit the same issue.

Hi everyone, thanks a lot for your input, based on the repros that @stephentoub  and myself provided.

Do we need more repros? If so, how can I help?
If we are ok with the repros that we have, would it be ok if I start a draft PR including the changes @JamesNK  and myself suggested?
I don't see a reason not to make the change here. Feel free to open a PR @danespinosa, thanks!
Triage: It is transport (NamedPipe) problem, but given that the fix is simple, we should just swap the read and write calls (while adding comment explaining the order requirement).

review_comments: Can you please add a comment here explaining that calling `ProcessIncoming` before `WriteAsync` is an intentional implementation detail to support named pipes?

How does this sound?

```csharp
// Processing the incoming frames before sending the client preface and SETTINGS is necessary when using a NamedPipe as a transport.
// If the preface and SETTINGS coming from the server are not read first, the below WriteAsync and the ProcessIncomingFramesAsync fall into a deadlock.
```

Also, there are 2 tests that I could clone and add a test with a NamedPipe stream.

ConnectCallback_ConnectionPrefix_Success clone and add **ConnectCallback_NamedPipeConnectionPrefix_Success**
ConnectCallback_UseUnixDomainSocket_Success clone and add **ConnectCallback_UseNamedPipeSocket_Success**

would that help? If the order of things ever change those tests could easily catch the issue.

That looks good to me.
The tests would be appreciated to prevent future regressions.

Hi @MihaZupan I have created a test that does detect the regresion, the only problem is that it does fail for HTTP1 since I didn't fix anything regarding HTTP1. So I guess the HTTP1 connection would need a similar fix. Should I work on that fix too or can the test target only http2 via a test attribute on the method?
IMO no one has asked for http/1.1 so leave it unchanged. Support can be added in the future when a need is identified.

I modified the test so it would only be part of the http2 test flow only.
If a regression gets introduced the ConnectCallback_UseNamedPipe_Success test would fail.
I have tested that by reverting my change and the test does detect the regression.
Just as an FYI I tested the new library on my test project and it works like a charm too :) Thanks a lot @MihaZupan  and @JamesNK  for your help
